prompt: Explain me compact operator in human words
response: A compact operator is like a machine that takes in functions and spits out other functions, but it has a special property. Imagine you have a bunch of functions, and you feed them all into this machine. The machine will process them, and you'll get a new set of functions out. The special property is that no matter how many functions you put in, the output functions will always be nicely behaved and won't be too spread out. This makes compact operators very useful in many areas of mathematics.
